subject: Argus: recommended GPU mix & cost-latency policy for Dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Argus sizing prep — initial SKU mix proposal

Team — drafting the note we'll send to Argus later today. High-level ask: we need a recommended Dedicated SKU mix that balances their heavy embed+rerank spikes (3x daily) and steady prompt traffic with 99th% latency target of 150ms for interactive flows. Key constraints from discovery:
- Token distribution: 70% short prompts (<64 tokens), 25% mid (<512), 5% long (>512) but long drives memory pressure for KV cache.
- Peak qps observed in demo: 120 qps; expected steady-state 30 qps.
- Budget guidance: prefer predictable monthly commit; they asked for unit-cost transparency.

My initial thought: L4 for baseline inference and embeddings (cost-effective, good for high qps, lower memory per instance), H100 for long-context, latency-sensitive model variants, and a small A100 pool to host 80GB FP16-heavy models that need large per-GPU memory for batch consolidation. But I think we should quantify: throughput per GPU, expected per-token cost, and a fallback policy (L4 warm cache + H100 for tail).

I've attached a quick workbook with modeled scenarios (argus-sku-modeling.xlsx). Can you each 1) validate the throughput numbers for the H100/A100/L4 rows, 2) call out critical operational risks (KV cache thrash, cold-starts, batch variance), and 3) confirm any recommended autoscale policy (target queue latency vs. spare capacity). I want to keep the external-facing note under one page.

— Rohan

Rohan — quick notes after scanning the workbook:

1) Throughput & cost assumptions (validated):
- L4 (q4): ~1,200 short-prompt completions/s per 8-GPU node when quantized; best for embeddings & bulk rerank when using 4-bit quantization and batching.
- A100 80GB: ~400 mid-length completions/s per 8-GPU node with larger batch consolidation; required for models that need >24GB activation memory.
- H100: ~650 completions/s for latency-tuned low-batch workloads and long-context workloads due to better tensor core perf.

2) Memory/perf tradeoffs to call out in external note (short bullets):
- A100 gives headroom for single-model large activation footprints (long-form generation + big KV cache).
- H100 gets better latency at small batch sizes (important for their interactive 99th%).
- L4 is the lowest-cost per-token but suffers when you need large on-GPU KV caches; consider L4 only for stateless inference or as a cache-hitting layer.

3) Ops risks / mitigations:
- KV cache thrash if we split routing naively between L4 and H100: mitigate with prefix-pin caching for interactive flows.
- Cold starts for H100-backed routes — pre-warm pools during peak windows (we can schedule pre-warm start at their 2x spike).
- Quantization QA: need 2% regression monitors in Redwood Optimize prior to rollout.

4) Autoscale policy suggestion (practical):
- Primary pool: L4 baseline sized to 1.5x steady qps to absorb spikes for low-cost requests.
- H100 reserved: sized to cover 60% of peak tail latency-sensitive QPS with autoscale up to 120% via burst capacity.
- A100 reserve: hot standby for long-context batch jobs; use A100 for scheduled nightly batch reranks.

I can trim into one-paragraph bullets for the external note. Ben — can you sanity-check the burst-to-reserve ratios?

—Marissa

Subject: Proposal: Dedicated GPU mix & cost-latency policy — Argus Therapeutics (summary)

Alex / Procurement — attaching a short summary and the modeling workbook we ran against your demo traces. TL;DR recommendation for an initial Dedicated commit (monthly):

- Baseline pool: 12 x L4 nodes (quantized) — handles 70% of short prompt traffic and bulk embedding workloads. Rationale: best cost-per-token for high qps; use for stateless embedding endpoints and bulk rerank.
- Tail / latency pool: 4 x H100 nodes — reserved to maintain 99th% <150ms for interactive flows and long-context generation. H100 has better small-batch latency and KV cache performance.
- Batch / memory pool: 2 x A100 80GB nodes — scheduled nightly for large reranks and any long-batch consolidation jobs that exceed L4 active memory.

Operational policy (key bullets):
- Routing: requests tagged by intent (embed | interactive | batch). Router sends embed->L4, interactive->H100 (fallback to L4 only when H100 unavailable), batch->A100.
- Cache pinning: interactive prefixes pinned to H100 KV caches for 90s after an active session to prevent cold misses.
- Autoscale: baseline L4 scaled to 1.5x steady (auto) with 2x burst throttle based on queue latency signal; H100 reserved with 1.2x burst enabled via prepaid burst credits.
- Cost transparency: we estimate blended unit cost of $0.00085/token at projected mix; detailed breakdown in attached PDF.

Attachments: argus-sku-modeling.xlsx, latency-cost-breakdown.pdf. Next steps: if this looks good I’ll generate an ops-runbook (pre-warm windows, alert thresholds) and a draft SLA language for the Dedicated contract.

Please reply with any redlines or if you want us to re-run the model with a higher long-context percentage.

Best,
Rohan

Thanks, Rohan — this is really helpful and very clear. A few quick notes from our side: 

- We like the split; L4-heavy baseline + small H100 tail sounds cost-effective.
- One ask: can we move one of the A100s to on-demand instead of reserved? We only run large reranks twice nightly; keeping one on-demand might save us cash on the committed line item.
- Would like more clarity on the degradation path if H100 capacity is exhausted (e.g., percent of requests that would fall back to L4 and expected P50/P95 change).

If you can update the workbook with an on-demand A100 option and a quick table showing fallback latency impact, we can sign off on the commit size. Also please include proposed pre-warm windows in the ops-runbook draft.

Appreciate the detail — will loop in procurement for contract items.
